question: The European Scientific Working group on Influenza is a European public health network organisation founded in 1992. Its core objective is reducing the impact of acute respiratory viral infections in Europe. It is financed by EU funds, scientific research funding and pharmaceutical companies (e.g. AstraZeneca, GSK, Sanofi).

Alongside the major respiratory viruses (such as influenza, RSV, COVID-19 and hMPV), its areas of focus include vaccination strategies, pandemic preparedness, the monitoring of viruses and health communication.

According to ChatGPT, the European Scientific Working group on Influenza has established itself over the years as an important voice in European influenza and pandemic policy, as an interface between science and policy and as a platform for awareness and communication. ChatGPT also states that the organisation’s role was bolstered particularly in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. 1.
Which tasks are carried out by the European Scientific Working group on Influenza that are not or cannot be performed by the EU administration?
In the past ten years, how much funding has the EU provided each year?
What specific tasks and role did this NGO fulfil during the COVID-19 pandemic and vaccination campaigns?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.8.2026) 1. The European Scientific Working Group on Influenza1 (ESWI) is a network organisation that aims to reduce the burden of influenza and other acute respiratory viruses in Europe. It organises conferences, roundtables, webinars, etc.

The EU administration proposes and implements laws, manages the EU budget, ensures policies are correctly applied, and represents the EU globally, all tasks that a network of academics cannot do. 2. The ESWI was a participant in the PREPARE project2 under the Seventh Framework programme for Research3.

The legal commitment was initially signed in 2013, and the project implementation took place between 1 February 2014 and 31 January 2021. ESWI’s anticipated EU funding under the grant was for an amount of EUR 80,362. 3. The Commission did not entrust any specific task or role to ESWI during the COVID-19 pandemic.
